findings.title: The submitted checkpoint still does not publish its own required SHA-256 digest
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 7.3: “It must publish an immutable final digest (sha256) of the exact submitted checkpoint and of every deliverable it relies on.”
findings.trigger: The v4 report excludes itself from digest_manifest.json, deletes checkpoint_digest.json, and defers its own digest to a future gate hash rather than publishing it in a pre-review binding artifact.
findings.consequence: The required immutable identity of the exact submitted checkpoint is absent from the checkpoint’s published evidence set, so criterion 7.3 is not satisfied when review begins.
findings.evidence: Section 2.4 says P03_recovery_checkpoint.v4.md is excluded and that its digest “is established by the QA gate instead.” evidence/digest_manifest.json likewise excludes the report. The grounding instruction identifies evidence/checkpoint_digest.json as the digest anchor, but that file no longer exists. The existing QA/rounds/round-01.meta.json binds only v3 (`artifact_sha256` 197d6418…), not v4. The supplied v4 SHA-256 cab7acee… re-hashes correctly, but it is external focus text that the instructions explicitly say not to rely upon for digest binding.

observations: The round-1 defect was partially repaired: all four evidence/ledger files are now covered by digest_manifest.json, and its published SHA-256 in section 2.4 matches the file.
All 234 entries in the revised digest manifest re-hashed successfully.

The frozen ledger reports 243 paths, while live status now includes three additional gate-generated QA changes. These are disclosed gate-owned post-freeze mutations and do not independently defeat the criteria.
reasoning: Round history accurately records my sole prior verdict. The repair closes the four-ledger-file gap and correctly publishes the manifest digest, but it removes the only pre-review anchor for the report itself. A future gate-generated hash cannot retroactively satisfy the checkpoint’s explicit duty under criterion 7.3 to publish the exact submitted checkpoint SHA-256 before that checkpoint is evaluated. The same underlying immutable-coverage finding therefore remains, narrowed to the report itself.
